key_insight: In a young-onset neuropsychiatry cohort, Alzheimer’s and psychiatric polygenic risk showed distinct disease associations, with no detected association with plasma biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: Genetic risk scores may capture information distinct from current pathology, but their added diagnostic value remains unproven.
method: Studied 687 European-ancestry participants: healthy controls, primary psychiatric disorders, Alzheimer’s disease and other neurodegenerative diseases.
Calculated five polygenic risk scores excluding the APOE locus; adjusted models for age, sex and APOE ε4 dose.
Assessed plasma NfL, GFAP and p-tau217 in 332 participants.
evidence_signal: Alzheimer’s and psychiatric risk scores were associated with their respective diagnoses versus controls (OR per SD 1.69 and 1.29); adding Alzheimer’s genetic risk to NfL changed discrimination between psychiatric and other neurodegenerative disorders only slightly (AUC 0.764 to 0.773).
watch_item: European-ancestry sampling limits generalizability, and larger longitudinal preclinical cohorts are needed to establish diagnostic utility.
paper_title: Alzheimers disease and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers in a real-world young-onset dementia cohort.
